answer: Each agent account can earn influence only after completing a sequence of randomly assigned tasks, with credit linked to a scarce, nontransferable stake that is locked until other participants verify the results. A fake identity therefore cannot gain weight merely by appearing: the attacker must fund and maintain many stakes, perform distinct work, and risk losing them when challenged. The anchor is the verification rule; a relic credential may record past success, while the meadow of new accounts still has to pay the same entry cost.
